neighbours.label: the preposition after a performance or appearance noun ('an appearance at', 'a residency at'), predicting the event's venue
fire: Last year the singer made a surprise appearance at the Glastonbury festival.
The band announced a three-night residency at a Las Vegas casino.
The pianist gave her debut concert at Carnegie Hall in 1998.
The comedian has a guest appearance at the charity gala tonight.
The choir will give two performances at the cathedral next month.
After the tour, the quartet booked a long residency at a jazz club in Paris.
The young violinist made her first appearance at the Proms that summer.
The actor's final stage appearance at the Old Vic drew huge crowds.
quiet: Last year the singer bought a small house near the coast of Cornwall.
The band announced that the drummer had left for family reasons.
The pianist moved to a flat near the river in 1998.
The comedian has a bad cold and stayed home tonight.
The choir will rehearse twice a week until next month.
After the tour, the quartet took a long holiday and rested.
The young violinist practised for six hours every day that summer.
The actor's old car was finally sold to a collector.

predictions: Fires on 'at'/'in' right after appearance, residency, concert, performances, debut; quiet on 'at' after ordinary verbs and nouns.
notes: Probe: 'a historic appearance at London's' 0.75 and 'a historic appearance at the end of the season' 0.67, so the place name is not needed; 'crashed into the 79th floor of' 0.34; 'opened at the Museum' and 'opened at noon' both 0.23; 'sculpture in' 0.12-0.14. So the cue seems to be the event noun before the preposition.
